A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of indoor residual spraying (IRS) combined with insecticide treated nets (ITNs) provides better malaria control than ITNs alone.
ITNs alone are more cost effective and more sustainable than IRS plus ITN.
the use of IRS, in combination with ITN, is a more effective strategy than ITN alone.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IRS is an effective malaria control intervention when combined with ITNs, and that this is a cost effective strategy.
the addition of indoor residual spraying to insecticide-treated bednets is unlikely to be cost-effective in the context of a malaria elimination programme.
